# parity-fuzz --mode stateful baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode stateful --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# The typeset-arith-error-exit (X) class is fixed (dispatch_builtin preserves
# the prior status on a soft math error in a BINF_ASSIGN builtin — see
# tests/parity/fuzz_discovered_parity.rs mod typeset_arith_error_exit).
#
# FIXED: nounset error inside a `[[ … ]]` operand now preserves the cond result
# (BUILTIN_COND_STATUS_FROM_BOOL syncs the conditional's lastval to the executor
# before ERREXIT_CHECK — see mod nounset_in_conditional).
#
# KNOWN-OPEN: after a prior `(( … ))`, the exit code of a following nounset
# error is context-dependent in zsh (2 vs the bare 1) whereas zshrs always
# yields 1 — a separate (non-conditional) facet of zsh's nuanced nounset
# exit-status propagation, still deferred.
print -r -- "${(t)iv}"
#
# KNOWN-OPEN: under `setopt KSH_ARRAYS`, a bare `${(flags)arr}` (no [@]/[*])
# is element 1 only, so a j/o/O/u/U/L flag operates on that single element
# (`${(j:-:)parts}` → `a`, not `a-b-c`). zshrs applies the flag to the full
# array — the flag/join path fetches the array independently of the KSHARRAYS
# bare-name collapse. Pinned #[ignore] in mod ksh_arrays_bare_flag_collapse.
parts=(a b c); joined=${(j:-:)parts}; print -r -- $joined
